question: Galician is used every day by thousands of people in Galicia but has still not been accepted as an official language of the European Union, in spite of the Spanish Government’s request to make Galician, Catalan and Basque EU official languages.

The fact that the people of my country cannot communicate with the EU in their own language reveals a deficit in legitimacy and democracy that undermines the image of the Union. Galician Literature Day is held on 17 May. Galicians celebrate figures who are important for their language and call for Galician to be used more widely in society.

Like every year, the 2026 event saw thousands of people protesting against the removal of Galician from education, culture and public services and a Galician Government that undermines our language. Public opinion is irrefutably against that policy. In view of the above: When will the Council allow Galician and the other official languages of Spain be official languages of the European Union?
answer: In 2006, the Council concluded an administrative arrangement with the Kingdom of Spain1 on the official use of additional languages whose status is recognised by the Constitution of the Kingdom of Spain in all or part of its territory, or the use of which as a national language is authorised by law.

Based on that arrangement, Spanish citizens may send to and receive from the Council written communication in Galician via the competent body designated for that purpose by the Spanish Government. Spanish representatives may also, under certain conditions, use such languages in speeches at Council meetings.

In addition, the Spanish Government may make certified translations into Galician of acts of the European Union adopted under the ordinary legislative procedure and forward them to the General Secretariat of the Council. Such certified translations are added by the Council to its archives. The Council provides copies of such translations on request to any citizen of the Union.
Moreover, in accordance with Article 55(2) of the Treaty on European Union, the Kingdom of Spain deposited in September 2011 a certified copy of the EU Treaties translated into Galician.
